t:
(a) Staff.—The Librarian may appoint and fix the pay of such personnel as the Librarian considers appropriate to carry out this title. 
    (b) Experts and Consultants.—The Librarian may, in carrying out this title, procure temporary and intermittent services under section 3109(b) of title 5, United States Code, but at rates for individuals not to exceed the daily equivalent of the maximum rate of basic pay payable for level 15 of the General Schedule. In no case may a member of the Board (including an alternate member) be paid as an expert or consultant under this section.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "Experts and Consultants" means outside experts are consulted before a federal decision. In fact this is a staffing and procurement authority: the Librarian may hire personnel and buy temporary services, which is paid work for the government, not a process for outside input on a decision. The reference to the Board only bars its members from being paid as consultants; it does not create or describe any advisory role in this section.
fable.s: The Librarian may, in carrying out this title, procure temporary and intermittent services under section 3109(b) of title 5, United States Code

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes the Librarian to hire temporary staff and consultants. While these individuals are outside the permanent federal workforce, the act of hiring employees or contractors to perform work for the government is not considered 'participation' in the sense of consulting with outside parties to inform a decision or involving them in a governance process. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and hiring is a similar administrative action rather than a participatory decision-making mechanism like a public hearing or advisory board consultation on policy.
qwen_block.s: The Librarian may, in carrying out this title, procure temporary and intermittent services under section 3109(b) of title 5, United States Code, but at rates for individuals not to exceed the daily equivalent of the maximum rate of basic pay payable for level 15 of the General Schedule.

opus.w: This section only lets the Librarian hire staff and pay for temporary experts and consultants under 5 U.S.C. 3109. Those people work for the government while they serve, so it is not outside participation. It might seem to count because it mentions outside 'experts and consultants' and a 'Board.' But the text sets up no consultation, comment period, hearing or advisory input on any federal decision. The reference to the Board only limits how its members can be paid.
opus.s: The Librarian may, in carrying out this title, procure temporary and intermittent services under section 3109(b) of title 5, United States Code
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** Subsection (b) lets the Librarian bring in outside "experts and consultants," and it mentions "a member of the Board," which in the wider law may be a board with outside members. That looks like outsiders being brought into decisions.
2. **Why it fails:** Section 3109 services are hired, paid, temporary federal employment. Like the paid board members in Example 7, these are government workers doing their jobs, not outsiders being consulted on a decision. The only mention of the Board stops its members from being paid as consultants. Nothing here creates a consultation, hearing, comment period or advisory role in a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the Librarian to hire temporary and intermittent services (consultants/experts). Hiring consultants is a procurement/contracting activity, not a participatory process where outside parties consult or coordinate with the government before a decision is made. The definition excludes applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses, and this falls under the umbrella of contracting for services rather than public participation in decision-making.
qwen_chat.s: The Librarian may, in carrying out this title, procure temporary and intermittent services under section 3109(b) of title 5, United States Code, but at rates for individuals not to exceed the daily equivalent of the maximum rate of basic pay payable for level 15 of the General Schedule.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that hiring "Experts and Consultants" constitutes participation because these are outside individuals providing input. However, the definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses, and hiring consultants is a form of contracting for services, not a participatory process in decision-making (like an advisory board or public comment). Furthermore, the text does not specify that these experts are part of a deliberative body influencing a specific federal decision in the manner described by the definition (e.g., advisory committee, consultation before a decision). It is merely an authorization to hire temporary staff.
